title: Reviewer verdict never reaches the orchestrator (it hangs at 'wait for review')
description: Dogfood 2026-06-23: after the sidecar dispatched the reviewer and the reviewer emitted <review>CLEAN</review> in its pane, the orchestrator sat idle at 'wait for review' forever; the operator had to tell it manually. Root cause = an asymmetry between the implementer and reviewer completion paths. The implementer has an exit-report (US-003): it writes worker-report.json AND send-keys a one-line summary to the orchestrator pane, so the orchestrator narrates it. The reviewer has NO exit-report: it only emits the <review> tag, which the SIDECAR detects by polling capture-pane (review.ts), and the supervisor never send-keys anything to the orchestrator pane (getOrchPaneId is used only by the thin-proxy CLI commands, never by the supervisor loop). So the sidecar detects CLEAN, updates prd.review and reaches terminal, but nothing hands the verdict back to the orchestrator, which hangs. Incomplete CAM-55 conversion (push-on-exit was applied to the implementer, not the reviewer). Fix: give the reviewer the same exit-report push the implementer has (write a report + send-keys the verdict line to the orchestrator pane), OR have the sidecar push the terminal verdict to the orchestrator on review-done. Acceptance: after a reviewer emits CLEAN/FIXES_PENDING the orchestrator receives the verdict in its pane and narrates it WITHOUT the operator intervening; a contract/integration test pins the reviewer->orchestrator hand-back. Relates to CAM-63 (supervisor<->worker boundary), CAM-65 (worker-pane close). Prerequisite for CAM-71. Source: dogfood observation.
